start.title: Coal
start.text: Burn coal for your first 40 FE/t. Run Copper Cable to an Electric Furnace and a Battery Box.

start.title: Steam
start.text: Make steel, then a Boiler with a Steam Turbine on top. A Sink next to the boiler gives it endless water; lava underneath heats it for free.

start.title: Processing
start.text: Double your ores with the Pulverizer, then triple them with the Ore Purifier. The Alloy Smelter makes Superconductor from copper and lithium.

start.title: Fission
start.text: Mine uranium, make Fuel Rods and build a Fission Reactor with a Sink for cooling water. Pipe its steam to turbines for extra power.

start.title: Fusion
start.text: Mine lithium below Y=0. Fill fuel cells in the Electrolyzer and light a compact Fusion Reactor with 1,000,000 FE.

start.title: Scale up
start.text: Build the multiblock Fusion Reactor and an Energy Bank, then automate everything with Item Pipes, a Quarry and a Chunk Loader.

categories.title: Power generation
categories.intro: From burning coal to splitting uranium to fusing hydrogen - with sun and wind along the way.

entries.text: Your first power source - smoke rises from its chimney while it burns. Burns any furnace fuel - coal, charcoal, planks, sawdust, other mods' fuels - and pushes power into cables and machines on every side.

Burns liquid fuel for power, 1 mB a tick: Biodiesel gives 200 FE/t, Rocket Fuel 300 FE/t, and Creosote Oil from the Coke Oven 40 FE/t - so even the early game's by-product makes power. Pipe the fuel in or pour a bucket in; it holds 200,000 FE, pushes power out of every side, and idles while full. Its grille glows while it runs.

Turns your crops into fuel. Seeds are pressed into plant oil (50 mB each - a sunflower gives 200), and sugary crops are fermented into ethanol: sugar 100 mB, sugar cane and pumpkins 80, apples 60, wheat and potatoes 50, carrots and beetroot 40, berries 30, melon slices 25, a honey bottle 150. It blends the two half and half into Biodiesel and pushes it out into Fluid Pipes (or take it with a bucket). 20 FE/t while working. Feed it both kinds of crop - from a greenhouse, say - and it never stops.
Free power in daylight when nothing blocks its view of the sky. Half power in rain, nothing at night. A low panel you can walk on; pushes power down and sideways into cables.
Made from 4 Solar Panels.
Made from 4 Advanced Solar Panels.
Made from 4 Elite Solar Panels.
Tier 5 solar: made from 4 Ultimate Solar Panels, Quantum Alloy and Quantum Cable.
Tier 6 solar: 36,000 FE/t in full sun - four times a Quantum Solar Panel. Solar Glass over four Quantum Solar Panels, a Naquadah Ingot and Quantum Cable.

Banks the power of thunderstorms. Put a vanilla Lightning Rod on top of it (or on one of its sides). During a thunderstorm the rod pulls in lightning from up to 128 blocks away, and every strike that hits it adds 2,500,000 FE to the collector in one go. It stores 25 million FE and feeds it out steadily at up to 20,000 FE/t on every side - one good storm can run a base for days. It glows for a few seconds after a strike, a comparator next to it reads how full it is, and the Multimeter shows how many strikes it has caught. A strike straight onto the collector counts too.

Wireless power - any distance, any dimension, no cable runs. Feed a Power Transmitter with cables on any side. Right-click it with a Wireless Linker, then right-click as many Power Receivers as you like to link them to it. Each Receiver draws power from its Transmitter and pushes it into the cables, machines and batteries around it. A Transmitter hands out up to 64,000 FE/t in total, shared between its receivers; each holds 1,000,000 FE as a buffer. Links within a dimension are lossless; across dimensions (power your Nether outpost from the Overworld) 10% is lost on the way. The chunks at both ends must be loaded - a Chunk Loader at each end makes it reliable. Jade shows what each end is doing.

Containers for gases. The Gas Tank is a tall pressure cylinder holding 64,000 mB of one gas: connect Gas Pipes to any side to fill it or draw from it, and break it to carry the gas away - it keeps its contents (shown on the item). Right-click it to see what's inside. The Gas Cylinder is the handheld version, like a real oxygen bottle: it holds 8,000 mB of one gas, and its coloured shoulder shows which. Right-click any machine, tank or Gas Tank with it to fill the cylinder from there - or, if it's full, to empty it in. Gases only; liquids use buckets and Fluid Tanks. The creative tab has a full cylinder of every gas for testing.

Wireless item and fluid transport - any distance, any dimension. Feed a Wireless Sender with pipes, hoppers or buses: it holds 9 stacks of items and 16,000 mB of one fluid or gas. Right-click it with a Wireless Linker, then right-click as many Wireless Receivers as you like. Each Receiver takes up to 32 items and 2,000 mB from its Sender twice a second and pushes them straight into the chests, machines, tanks and pipes next to it. Ship ore home from a remote quarry, send fuel to an outpost, or move gas between dimensions. The chunks at both ends must be loaded (a Chunk Loader helps); Jade shows each end's state.
The other end of a Wireless Sender: link it with a Wireless Linker (right-click the Sender first). It pulls items and fluid from its Sender and pushes them into everything next to it.

A queue between machines. It takes items in from any side except its front (27 slots) and steadily pushes them out of the front - 16 items every 4 ticks - into a pipe, machine or chest. Put one between a fast producer and a slow machine so the producer never stalls. The front (with the arrow) faces the way you look when you place it.
The fluid version of the Item Buffer: holds 32,000 mB of one fluid or gas, filled from any side except the front, and pushes 1,000 mB a tick out of the front.

Calls a thunderstorm when you want one. Once it holds 4,000,000 FE and has a Storm Charge in its slot, it uses both to start a 5-minute storm - only in dimensions with weather, and never while it's already storming, so charges aren't wasted. It follows its redstone setting: on Always it storms as soon as it can; set it to need a signal and use a lever, or a comparator on a Lightning Collector, to call storms only when the collectors run low. Takes power through the bottom like other machines.
Fuel for the Storm Caller - one per storm. Made from a ghast tear, copper and redstone.

Free power from heat, no fuel needed. Every lava SOURCE block touching it - on any of its six sides - gives 20 FE/t (up to 120 FE/t), and every magma block 5 FE/t. Build it into a lava lake, or surround it with placed lava. Flowing lava doesn't count.

Cheap, always-on power from moving water. Every side (north, south, east, west) with FLOWING water next to it gives 8 FE/t, up to 32 FE/t; still water doesn't turn it. Its paddles spin while it works. Great for a river base or a little stream from a water source.

A big three-blade rotor that spins while it makes power. The higher you build it, the more it makes: nothing at sea level (Y 64), rising to full power (128 FE/t) at Y 256. Rain gives x1.5 and thunderstorms x2. Blocks within 3 blocks of it slow it down, so put it on a hill or tower with open space. Its GUI shows height, weather and how open the space is.

Boils water into steam for Steam Turbines. Heat comes from any furnace fuel or lava in its tank (full speed), or free from lava, magma, fire or a lit campfire directly underneath (half speed). Water comes from a Sink, Pump, pipes, tanks or buckets. Steam goes straight into a turbine on top, or out through Gas Pipes on any side to turbines anywhere.
Turns steam into power. Place it on top of a Boiler, or feed it steam through Gas Pipes. It spins up over about 5 seconds and outputs power on every side except the bottom.

The brain of the Industrial Turbine, a multiblock steam turbine that grows with its size. Build a hollow box from 3x3x3 up to 13x13x13: Turbine Casing on the edges and corners; Casing, Turbine Glass and Turbine Valves on the walls, with this controller in one wall; Turbine Rotors (and air) inside. Pipe steam into a valve. Each rotor passes 200 mB/t of steam, and more rotors make each mB worth more: x1.3 with one rotor up to x2 with 15 or more (at the default 2 FE per mB, that's up to 4 FE per mB). The steam condenses back into water (1 mB per 10 mB of steam), which the valves push out, so you can pipe it back to your boilers. Right-click the controller to see what's missing if it won't form.
Frame and walls of the Industrial Turbine. Edges and corners must be casing.
See-through wall for the Industrial Turbine, to watch the blades spin.
Goes in an Industrial Turbine wall: takes steam in, and pushes power and condensed water out into whatever touches it. Cables and pipes can also pull from it.
A shaft section for the inside of an Industrial Turbine. Each one lets 200 mB/t of steam through and raises the turbine's efficiency. Its blades appear and spin once the turbine forms.

The compact, single-block fission generator - and the core ingredient of the Fission Controller for the multiblock reactor. Burns up to 4 Uranium Fuel Rods (5 minutes each; they come back as Depleted Fuel Rods). Output rises with heat and is full at 50%. Above that it cools itself with water from a Sink, Pump or pipes - and the water flashes to steam, which it pushes into Gas Pipes or Steam Turbines for bonus power. Without water it overheats and SCRAMs (shuts itself down until cool). Meltdown explosions are off unless you turn them on in the config. Two add-ons work with it: a Tritium Breeder next to it turns lithium into tritium for fusion, and a Cryo Injector fed with nitrogen gives +50% power. It burns MOX Fuel Rods too: twice as long, 50% more power and heat.
Makes fusion fuel. Empty Fuel Cell + water gives a Deuterium Cell; Empty Fuel Cell + Lithium Ingot gives a Tritium Cell. Pulls water from anything next to it.

The compact, single-block reactor. Charge it with 1,000,000 FE, load a Deuterium and a Tritium cell and it ignites. Each pair burns for 2 minutes. If fuel runs out it cools over about 25 seconds - refuel in time or it needs re-igniting. Also the core ingredient of the multiblock Fusion Controller. It also runs on gas: pipe in deuterium (from an Isotope Separator) and tritium (from a Tritium Breeder) - 250 mB of each lasts as long as one pair of cells, and gas is burned before cells. Plasma Coils (Mk I-III) raise its output up to x4.

categories.title: Fusion Reactor multiblock
categories.intro: The end-game generator. Any box from 3x3x3 to 13x13x13; every Magnet Coil inside adds output.

entries.text: Brain of the multiblock Fusion Reactor. Build a hollow box (any size from 3x3x3 to 13x13x13), put the controller into a side wall facing out, fill the inside with Magnet Coils and right-click the controller. If something's wrong it names the exact block and position. Gas works here too: pipe deuterium and tritium into the controller - 250 mB of each per fuel pair, burned before cells. Plasma Coils (Mk I-III) raise its output up to x4, and a Reactor Gauge can be built into its walls.
entries.note: Structure: a hollow box from 3x3x3 to 13x13x13. Edges and corners: Reactor Casing. Walls: casing, Reactor Glass, at least one Fuel Port and one Power Port, and the controller facing out. Inside: Magnet Coils or air. Reactors with more than 27 coils burn fuel faster.

entries.text: The frame of the Fusion Reactor. Every edge and corner must be casing; the flat walls can also be glass or ports.
See-through wall block for the Fusion Reactor, so you can watch the coils glow. Walls only - not edges or corners.
Fills the inside of the Fusion Reactor. Each coil adds 1,500 FE/t to the reactor's output. Coils light up and ripple with plasma while the reactor runs.
Wall block of the Fusion Reactor. Hoppers, pipes and machines put Deuterium and Tritium cells in here and take the empty cells out. You need at least one.
Wall block of the Fusion Reactor. Feed ignition power in here while the reactor is off; once running it pushes power out into cables. Big reactors need several ports and Netherite or Quantum Cable.

categories.title: Fission Reactor multiblock
categories.intro: Scale fission up: any box from 3x3x3 to 13x13x13, where the way you arrange fuel and coolant decides how much power you get.

entries.text: Brain of the multiblock Fission Reactor. Build a hollow box (3x3x3 to 13x13x13) of Fission Casing, put the controller in a side wall facing out, and put at least one Fuel Assembly inside. Once it forms, water from the Coolant Port floods the empty space around the rods - you can watch them glowing underwater through the glass. Feed fuel rods through a Fuel Port (or the controller's GUI, which stores up to 64). The ports only work once the reactor has formed - right-click the controller to check. MOX Fuel Rods work here too (burned first): twice as long, 50% more power and heat.
stats: 5 + 2 per water block + 10 per Coolant Channel heat/t

entries.text: Frame of the multiblock Fission Reactor. Edges and corners must be casing. Green hazard stripes.
See-through wall block for the Fission Reactor - watch the fuel glow.

Goes inside the Fission Reactor. Makes up to 1,000 FE/t at full heat and adds 1 heat per tick. Every other assembly touching it adds +10% efficiency. One fuel rod lasts 6,000 assembly-ticks, so 10 assemblies use a rod every 30 seconds. Glows and pulses while the reactor runs.
Optional, inside the Fission Reactor. Each channel removes 10 heat per tick - five times what a water block does - so it's the compact way to cool a large core.
Wall block: fuel rods go IN. Right-click it holding rods to load them, or feed it with hoppers and Item Pipes. Right-click with an empty hand to see how many rods are loaded (up to 64).

Optional wall block: pushes depleted rods OUT into an Item Pipe, chest or hopper next to it. Pipe them to a Pulverizer to get uranium back for new rods. Without one, depleted rods wait in the controller's output slot.
Wall block: water in (Sink, Pump, Fluid Pipes) - it first floods the inside of the reactor - and steam out into Gas Pipes or Steam Turbines beside it.
Wall block: pushes the reactor's power into cables.

categories.title: Energy storage
categories.intro: Batteries for everyday use, and the Energy Bank multiblock for storing billions of FE.

entries.text: Stores power. The face pointing at you when placed is the Input; the other five faces are Outputs. Shift + right-click a face with an empty hand (or right-click with the Wrench) to cycle it Input / Output / Disabled. Keeps its energy when mined. Comparators read how full it is.
Bigger, faster Battery Box. Same face controls. Crafting it from a Battery Box doesn't carry the energy over - drain it first.
Elite tier Battery Box.
The largest single-block battery.
Tier 5: the largest single-block battery, holding two billion FE.

Brain of the Energy Bank - multiblock storage built like the Fusion Reactor. Any box from 3x3x3 to 13x13x13, controller in a side wall, Energy Cells inside. The GUI shows stored energy, capacity and live in/out rates. Breaking the structure keeps the energy; nothing flows until it's rebuilt.
entries.note: Structure: a hollow box from 3x3x3 to 13x13x13. Edges and corners: Bank Casing. Walls: Bank Casing, Bank Glass, at least one Bank Port, and the controller facing out. Inside: Energy Cells (any mix) or air.

entries.text: The end-game power store, made for satellite and antimatter output. A steel cage with a glowing orb inside: the orb grows, brightens and spins faster as the core fills, and changes colour with each tier. Tier I holds 20 billion FE; Core Upgrades raise it to 100 billion, 1 trillion, 10 trillion and finally 100 trillion FE (tier V) - right-click the core with them, in order. The core has no connections of its own: place Input Pylons (feed them with cables) and Output Pylons (they push power into anything touching them) within 8 blocks and they link to it by themselves, with sparks running along the link while power flows. Each pylon moves 1M FE/t at tier I, rising to 256M FE/t at tier V - add more pylons for more throughput. It keeps its tier and energy when you break it, a comparator reads how full it is, and right-clicking it or any of its pylons shows the charge and the flow.
Feeds an Energy Core: power from cables on any side goes into the nearest core within 8 blocks, at that core tier's pylon rate.
Draws from the nearest Energy Core within 8 blocks and pushes the power into every cable, machine or battery touching it, at the core tier's pylon rate.

Core Upgrades raise an Energy Core one tier at a time - right-click the core with the next one: II (100 billion FE, 4M FE/t per pylon), III (1 trillion, 16M), IV (10 trillion, 64M), V (100 trillion, 256M). Each upgrade is made from the one before it.
Frame of the Energy Bank. Edges and corners must be casing. Yellow hazard stripes so it's easy to tell from reactor casing.
See-through wall block for the Energy Bank.

Wall block of the Energy Bank. Input (blue arrow) accepts power; Output (orange arrow) pushes power into cables. Shift + right-click with an empty hand, or use the Wrench, to switch. Add more ports for more throughput.
Goes inside the Energy Bank. Tiers can be mixed.
Goes inside the Energy Bank.
Goes inside the Energy Bank.
Tier 5 cell for the Energy Bank - eight times an Ultimate cell. Made from 4 Ultimate Energy Cells.

categories.title: Cables and pipes
categories.intro: Everything moves on networks: all connected pieces share the load, so length never matters.

entries.text: Carries Forge Energy - works with any mod that uses FE (Mekanism, Thermal, Powah, AE2...). All connected cables act as one network and share power fairly, however long the run. Each connection to a machine is limited by the cable tier touching it; tiers can be mixed. Cables are see-through: a glowing yellow line runs through them while power is flowing, and goes dark when the line is idle.
Mid-tier cable. Cables are see-through: a glowing yellow line runs through them while power is flowing, and goes dark when the line is idle.
High-tier cable. Cables are see-through: a glowing yellow line runs through them while power is flowing, and goes dark when the line is idle.
Top-tier cable, for fusion reactors and Energy Banks. Cables are see-through: a glowing yellow line runs through them while power is flowing, and goes dark when the line is idle.

Tier 5 cable: sixteen times Netherite. For full-size fusion reactors, Quantum Battery Boxes and big Energy Banks. Made from 8 Netherite Cable around a Quantum Alloy Ingot. Cables are see-through: a glowing yellow line runs through them while power is flowing, and goes dark when the line is idle.

Carries liquids (water, lava, other mods' liquids). Connected pipes form one network carrying one fluid at a time. Pipes push into the tanks and machines they touch; Wrench a connection to cycle Push / Pull (orange ring) / Push + Pull / Disabled.
Advanced liquid pipe.
Elite liquid pipe.
Ultimate liquid pipe.
Tier 5 liquid pipe.

Carries gases - fluids lighter than air, such as Steam. Use it to pipe steam from Boilers to Steam Turbines anywhere. Doesn't connect to liquid pipes. (Mekanism's gases use their own system and need Mekanism's tubes.)
Advanced gas pipe.
Elite gas pipe.
Ultimate gas pipe.
Tier 5 gas pipe - enough for a large reactor's steam.

Moves items between inventories - chests, machines, Storage Drawers, AE2 ME Interfaces, Refined Storage Interfaces, Sophisticated Storage. Items pushed in (by a machine's auto-output or a hopper) are delivered to the other inventories on the network, never back into the sender, and you can watch them glide along the pipes. Wrench a connection to cycle Push / Pull / Push + Pull / Disabled - a Pull only moves items when another connection on the network is set to Push. Right-click a connection with an empty hand to set its priority (0-9): higher priorities fill first, equal ones share.
Advanced item pipe.
Elite item pipe.
Ultimate item pipe.
Tier 5 item pipe.

Right-click the air to set up to 9 items, choose Allow or Block, and choose how to match: Item (exactly those items), Tag (anything sharing a tag - one raw ore matches all raw ores, one log matches all logs) or Mod (anything from the same mod). Right-click an Item Pipe connection with it to install it; shift + right-click the connection with an empty hand to take it off. A delivering connection then only accepts matching items; a pulling connection only pulls them. Its Name mode matches items whose id starts with the same word as the filter item - a deepslate iron ore matches every deepslate_... item.

Picks which fluids and gases a pipe connection lets through. Right-click it in the air to set it up: click its 9 slots with a bucket or tank of each fluid, and choose Allow (only these) or Block (everything but these). Then right-click a fluid or gas pipe where it connects to a machine or tank to install it, and sneak + right-click there with an empty hand to take it off. On a Pull connection it chooses what's pulled out - handy for taking just the hydrogen out of an electrolyzer that holds several gases; on a Push connection it chooses what's delivered. Filters drop out if the pipe is broken.

The ultimate mining tool: a drill, shovel, axe and hoe in one, mining very fast and digging a 1x1, 3x3, 5x5 or 7x7 area on whichever face you look at - shift + right-click to switch. It stores 50,000,000 FE and uses 400 FE per block, so a full charge lasts for well over a hundred thousand blocks. Charge it in a Charger or near a Wireless Charger. Made from an Advanced Drill, Quantum Alloy and a Quantum Power Core.

Carries dropped items along in the direction it faces (away from you when placed) - you can watch everything move. Mobs and players ride it too (sneak to stand still). At the end of a belt, items go into any chest, machine or pipe in front of it; hoppers, pipes and Export Buses can put items onto a belt. Sneak + right-click with an empty hand to make it a slope that goes up a block, then down a block, then flat again. Items on belts don't despawn.
A Conveyor Belt at twice the speed: 2.5 blocks per second. Works the same way - slopes with sneak + right-click.
The fastest belt: 5 blocks per second. Works the same way - slopes with sneak + right-click.

Items reaching the middle go out left, straight on and right in turn - only to sides with a belt or an inventory. Use it to feed a row of machines from one belt. Runs at Express speed so it never holds a belt back.

Items in its filter turn off to the left (sneak + right-click with an empty hand to switch to the right); everything else goes straight on. Right-click with an item to add it to the filter, again to take it out (up to 9 items); right-click with an empty hand to see the filter. Runs at Express speed.

categories.title: Processing machines
categories.intro: Powered machines take their power through the BOTTOM - run your cable underneath (the Electric Pump and Quarry take power on any side). The other five faces are for items: open the Sides window (cube button, top-right of the GUI) to set each face - Front, Back, Left, Right and Top, as you see the machine standing in front of it - to In, Out, both or off. Out faces hand over finished items to pipes, Import Buses and hoppers; In faces accept items. Every machine also has redstone control and auto-output. Most take Speed and Energy upgrade cards (up to 8 each) in their Upgrades window - the green arrow button - where you also see the machine's Muffler and tier. Tier Installers turn the Furnace, Pulverizer, Alloy Smelter, Compressor, Sawmill, Ore Purifier, Rock Crusher and Fluid Mixer into machines that run 3, 5, 7 or 9 operations at once.

entries.text: Early-game heavy industry - no power needed, the coal heats itself. Put coal in and it bakes into Coal Coke in 30 seconds, giving off 250 mB of Creosote Oil; logs become charcoal plus 125 mB of Creosote in 15 seconds. Coal Coke burns twice as long as coal in any furnace or generator, and turns iron into steel in the Industrial Blast Furnace. Take the Creosote Oil out with a pipe or an empty bucket; eight planks around a Creosote Oil Bucket make 8 Treated Planks. The front glows while it's working.

Steel before you have any power: an iron ingot and a Coal Coke (from a Coke Oven) become a steel ingot in 20 seconds - no fuel or power needed. Feed iron and coke in from the top or sides; steel comes out of the bottom.
Smelts anything a furnace can, using power instead of fuel.
Grinds ores and raw ores into 2 dusts - ore doubling. Smelt the dusts into ingots.
Washes ores and raw ores with water into 3 dusts - ore tripling. Put a Sink next to it for endless water.

The top tier of ore processing. Chlorine dissolves the metal out of an ore, giving 4 dust per ore or raw ore - one more than the Ore Purifier and double the Pulverizer. Each ore takes 100 mB of chlorine and 500 mB of water, 6 seconds at 300 FE/t. It works on every ore the Ore Purifier handles, including other mods' ores and raw ores. Takes Speed and Energy upgrades and Tier Installers, so a Quantum Chemical Washer handles 9 ores at a time. The chain: water -> Salt Evaporator -> salt -> Brine Electrolyzer -> chlorine (and hydrogen) -> Chemical Washer. It also reprocesses Depleted Fuel Rods into Plutonium Dust for MOX fuel.

Makes chlorine for the Chemical Washer by passing current through salt water: each salt plus 500 mB of water becomes 250 mB of chlorine and 250 mB of hydrogen, in 2 seconds at 200 FE/t. It pushes both gases out into Gas Pipes - send the chlorine to your washers and burn the hydrogen in a Gas Burner Generator to win some power back.

Boils water down to salt: 1,000 mB of water makes 1 salt in 5 seconds at 40 FE/t. Give it water from a Sink, an Electric Pump or pipes, and take the salt out with a pipe, a bus or auto-output. One evaporator keeps a Brine Electrolyzer busy about two-fifths of the time.
Salt from a Salt Evaporator. A Brine Electrolyzer turns it into chlorine. Tagged forge:dusts/salt, so other mods' salt works too.

Combines two inputs into an alloy. Inputs can go in either slot. With pipes or buses, feed both ingredients in through In faces - from the same pipe or different ones: each ingredient goes into its own slot, and items that don't make a recipe with what's loaded are refused, so it can't jam.
Presses items: ingots into plates, 8 coal blocks into a diamond, and more.
Cuts logs into 6 planks plus sawdust (crafting only gives 4), and planks into sticks.

Crushes the blocks you put in. It also breaks any ore block - normal or deepslate - into raw materials: 2 Raw Iron, Raw Gold, Raw Uranium or Raw Lithium, 5 Raw Copper, or the ore's gems, redstone, lapis, coal, quartz or netherite scrap.

Compresses 9 Ice into Packed Ice and 9 Packed Ice into Blue Ice. With nothing to compress it freezes its tank: 1,000 mB water gives Ice, 1,000 mB lava gives Obsidian. Pulls water or lava from neighbours. Takes Tier Installers: 3, 5, 7, 9 or 12 at once.

Charges any Forge Energy item from any mod - tools, armour, jetpacks, batteries. Fully charged items move to the output slot so a hopper can collect them. In autocrafting it can charge items as a step: make a charging pattern (the item as input, the same item as output, then press the Charge button in the Pattern Encoder) and give it to a Molecular Assembler touching the Charger. The item goes in, comes back fully charged and the craft carries on.

categories.title: Utility machines
categories.intro: Enchanting, mob farming, mixing, condensing and teleporting. Like the processing machines, they take power through the bottom and use the Sides window (faces as you see them from the front) for items.

entries.text: Enchants with power instead of your XP. Put an enchantable item (or a book) in the left slot and lapis in the middle, then pick level 10, 20 or 30 with the button. Books come out as enchanted books. Give it Liquid Experience (by pipe, bucket or a Mob Grinder next to it) and it enchants on XP instead of power, twice as fast - 40 mB per enchantment level, so a level-30 enchant uses 1,200 mB.

Experience as a liquid: 20 mB holds one experience point. A Mob Grinder turns the XP from its kills into Liquid Experience and pushes it into tanks and machines next to it; pipe it to an Enchanting Machine to enchant without power, or store it in any Fluid Tank. It can be carried in buckets and glows faintly if poured out.

Attacks mobs in a 5x3x5 area in front of it, as if a player hit them - so they drop player-only loot and XP. Drops go into its buffer (auto-output and pipes work); XP is stored - click the XP button in its GUI to take it. Choose hostile only or all mobs. It never harms players, bosses, name-tagged mobs, tamed pets or armour stands. It also turns the XP it collects into Liquid Experience (20 mB per point) and pushes it into tanks and machines next to it - put an Enchanting Machine beside it and it enchants on mob XP.

Place it touching a vanilla mob spawner. While powered, the spawner works without a player nearby and spawns faster and more mobs at a time (Speed Upgrades push it further). Without power it goes back to normal. Put a Mob Grinder in front of the spawner for a complete mob farm.

Mixes fluids with items: concrete powder + water gives concrete (any colour), dirt + water gives mud, and with the slot empty, lava + water gives obsidian. Pulls water and lava from a Sink, Pump, pipes or tanks.

Turns steam back into water (10 mB of steam makes 1 mB of water), up to 1,000 mB of steam per tick, with no power. Takes steam from Gas Pipes, Boilers or reactors next to it and pushes the water into anything that takes water - put it next to a Fission Reactor's Coolant Port for a closed water loop.

Right-click a pad with an empty hand to give it a name and pick where it sends you - every pad in the world is listed, even in other dimensions. Then stand on the pad and crouch to travel. Uses power from the pad you leave from.
A shortcut: right-click one Teleporter pad, then another, and they're linked both ways. (You can also pick destinations from a pad's own screen.)

categories.title: Item storage network
categories.intro: Put every item, fluid and gas you own in one searchable place, AE2-style but with no channels to worry about. Build a Storage Controller, power it, link Drive Bays full of Storage Disks and a Storage Terminal with Storage Cable, and open the terminal. Item Pipes can feed the controller directly.

entries.text: The heart of an item storage network. Link Drive Bays and Storage Terminals to it with Storage Cable (or place them touching it). Power it with a normal energy cable. Only one controller per network - two and the network switches off. It also works as one big inventory: point an Item Pipe into it to store things automatically, or pull items out of it with a pipe or hopper. Right-click it to see its status.
Links the parts of a storage network together: Storage Controller, Drive Bays and Storage Terminals. It carries no power or items itself - the controller still needs an energy cable.
Holds 8 Storage Disks. It glows when its network is online. Its screen shows how full the disks inside are.

Sets up your disks. Put a Storage or Fluid Disk in, then click items into its 18 partition slots - the disk will then only accept those items (an empty partition takes anything). For a Fluid Disk, click the slots with a bucket or tank of each fluid. Fill partitions the disk to exactly what's already stored on it; Clear removes the partition. Priority runs from -9 to +9: when items are stored, higher-priority disks are filled first, and at the same priority a disk partitioned for the item beats a general one. So make an ores disk at priority +1 and the rest at 0, and ores always land on it. Everything is saved on the disk, so it keeps its setup in any Drive Bay.

Locks a storage network. Place it anywhere on the network: whoever places it becomes the owner, and right-clicking it lets them add or remove trusted players by name (anyone who has joined the server, online or not). Everyone else can't open the network's terminals, Drive Bays, buses, assemblers or Stock Keeper, can't use or link wireless terminals to it, can't break its blocks, and can't place storage parts, pipes or other inventories against it. Only the owner can break the Security Terminal. Server operators can always get in. A network without one stays open to everyone.

A screen for your storage. Connect it to the network (touching a Storage Cable or another storage block) and right-click it with any item: its face shows that item and how many the network holds, updating live - green when you have some, red at zero. Right-click with an empty hand to read the exact count; sneak + right-click with an empty hand to clear it. A comparator reads the stock: 0 at none, then one more per doubling (1, 2, 4, 8 ... 16,384+ = 15), so a comparator and a redstone torch make a low-stock alarm - or wire it to a machine to make more when you run low.

Simple rules for a smart base, no redstone circuits needed. Connect it to your storage network and open it: each of its 4 rules reads IF something THEN give a redstone signal out of a side (North, South, East, West, Up, Down or all of them). Item: how many of an item the network holds is below or above a number - click the item into the rule's slot. Power: how full the batteries touching the controller are, in percent (Battery Boxes, an Energy Bank port, an Energy Core pylon). Redstone: the controller itself is getting a signal. Set the machines beside it to run on a redstone signal and they switch on and off by themselves - for example IF Iron Ingot < 1,000 THEN signal East, with a Pulverizer to the east; or IF power > 90% THEN signal Up to start a Particle Collider only when there's spare power. Each rule has a light that's lit while it's true; hover it to see the current reading. Rules are checked twice a second.

Sends the redstone signal going into it over one of 64 channels - any distance, any dimension (while its chunk is loaded). Right-click to pick the channel, sneak + right-click to go back. Its red light shows when it's sending.

Gives out the strongest signal any transmitter is sending on its channel (1-64), to all sides and through the block it's on. Right-click to pick the channel, sneak + right-click to go back. Pair it with a Logic Controller, a Machine Status Display's comparator output or a lever across the base - or the Stargate DHD's redstone dialling, from anywhere.

Right-click for a list of every machine within 24 blocks and what it's doing: Working, Idle, Blocked (it has items but isn't running - output full or something missing), No power, or Off (paused by redstone). Problems are listed first; filter by clicking the chips at the top. Its screen glows green when all is well, amber when something is blocked and red when something is out of power, and a comparator next to it gives the number of machines that need attention.
stats: Working, Idle, Blocked, No power, Off

entries.text: The controller of a multiblock ore factory. Build Factory Cells onto it - touching it or each other, any shape, up to 16 - and every cell runs 4 operations at once (up to 64 per cycle; a cycle takes 5 seconds, faster with Speed upgrades). Modes: Smelt (furnace recipes), Crush (like the Pulverizer: 2 dust per ore), Wash (like the Ore Purifier: 3 dust per ore, 250 mB water each) and Ore to Ingots (washes, then smelts the dust: 3 ingots per ore). Nine input and nine output slots; 20 FE/t per operation smelting, 40 crushing, 60 washing and 80 for Ore to Ingots - the same as the separate machines. Water, power and items go into the controller or any Factory Port on the structure.
stats: Smelt, Crush, Wash, Ore to Ingots
20 / 40 / 60 / 80 FE/t per operation (Smelt / Crush / Wash / Ore to Ingots)

entries.text: Part of a Digital Factory: place it touching the controller or another cell (any shape). Each cell adds 4 operations at once, up to 16 cells (64 at once).

Part of a Digital Factory: place it touching the controller or a cell. Pipes, cables and hoppers on a port reach the controller - items in go to the input slots, items out come from the output slots, and water and power flow in.

Shows everything stored in the network in one searchable grid. Click to take a stack, right-click to take half, shift-click to send it straight to your inventory. Click the grid while holding an item to store it (right-click stores just one), or shift-click items in your inventory to store them. Fluids and gases show too (amounts in buckets): hold an empty bucket or tank and click a fluid to fill it, or click the grid with a full one to pour it in. Type to search by name, or @modname for one mod. The All / Items / Fluids button picks what to show; 123 / A-Z switches the sort. While the network is crafting, a live queue beside the terminal shows each job's item, amount and crafts left.

A flat Storage Terminal for walls, floors and ceilings, like AE2's. Place it on a Storage Cable or any storage block; the screen faces away from the surface you click. Craft it from a Storage Terminal block, and back again.

A Storage Terminal with a 3x3 crafting grid underneath. Craft straight from storage: when a craft uses up a grid slot it refills from storage, so shift-clicking the result crafts as many as your stored materials allow. The x button (or closing the terminal) puts the grid back into storage. With JEI, open any crafting recipe and press + to fill the grid from storage; shift + fills a stack of each. Missing ingredients show in red. Craft All Missing: after JEI's + fills the grid, a + button under the grid's x starts crafting jobs for every ingredient storage was missing, and fills them into the grid as they're made.
A flat Crafting Terminal. Works exactly like the block version. Craft it from a Crafting Terminal block (and back), or from a Storage Terminal Panel plus a crafting table.

Moves things FROM the block it faces INTO storage. Place it against a chest, furnace, machine or tank (it faces the block you click on) and connect it to the network with Storage Cable. It takes items, fluids and gases. Right-click to set a filter; with an empty filter it takes everything. To filter a fluid, click a filter slot with a bucket or tank of it. The screen shows whether it's connected to a powered network.
stats: 8 items or 8 buckets every half second

entries.text: Moves things FROM storage INTO the block it faces - it never takes anything out of that block. Right-click and set what to send: items, or a bucket/tank for a fluid or gas. With an empty filter it sends nothing. Good for keeping a Pulverizer fed with ore, a Coal Generator topped up with coal, or a Steam Turbine supplied with stored steam.
stats: 8 items or 8 buckets every half second

entries.text: A doorway into storage from anywhere on the Storage Cable. Anything next to it - Item Pipes, Fluid and Gas Pipes, machines, reactors, hoppers - can push items, fluids and gases into storage or pull them out, as if it were one huge chest and tank. Put one next to a Fission Reactor to store its steam, and an Export Bus on a Steam Turbine elsewhere to use it.

Your storage in your hand. Sneak + right-click a Storage Controller to link it, then right-click anywhere within 64 blocks (in the same dimension) to open a full Storage Terminal - items, fluids, search and all. It runs on FE, using a little while it's open; charge it in a Charger, Wireless Charger or Portable Battery. Set the Open Wireless Terminal key in Controls > Key Binds > Tiered Industries and you can open it straight from your inventory.

A Wireless Terminal with a crafting grid: craft from storage wherever you are, with auto-refill and the JEI + button, just like the Crafting Terminal. Make it from a Wireless Terminal and a crafting table.

Extends your wireless terminals' reach. Put it anywhere on the storage network (touching Storage Cable or another storage block) and Wireless Terminals work within 128 blocks of it, as well as 64 blocks of the controller. Place a few to cover a big base or reach your mining area. The tip glows while the network is online.
Stores items for the network - put it in a Drive Bay. Everything stays on the disk if you take it out, so you can move a disk to another network. The bar under the disk shows how full it is.
Four times the 4K disk.
Four times the 16K disk.
The biggest disk - enough for a few full chests of every common block.
Holds 1,048,576 items - four 256K disks in one. Made from 4 Storage Disks (256K), superconductor and a nether star.
Holds 4,194,304 items in one drive bay slot. Made from 4 Storage Disks (1M), Quantum Alloy and a Quantum Power Core.
Stores fluids and gases for the network - water, lava, steam, hydrogen, oxygen and other mods' fluids. Put it in a Drive Bay alongside item disks. Contents stay on the disk when you take it out.
Four times the 4K fluid disk.
Four times the 16K fluid disk.
The biggest fluid disk - room for a reactor's worth of steam.
Holds 1,048,576 buckets of fluids and gases - four 256K disks in one. Made from 4 Fluid Storage Disks (256K), superconductor and a nether star.

Holds 4,194,304 buckets of fluids and gases: an endgame tank for steam, deuterium, oxygen or rocket fuel in a single drive bay slot. Made from 4 Fluid Storage Disks (1M), Quantum Alloy and a Quantum Power Core.

categories.title: Autocrafting
categories.intro: Ask your storage for something it can make and it crafts it for you - including the parts along the way. 1) Encode patterns in a Pattern Encoder - crafting recipes, or processing (machine) recipes. 2) Put them in a Molecular Assembler on the storage network; for processing patterns, place that assembler against the machine. 3) Add a Crafting CPU. The planner chains everything: ask for Superconductor Ingots and it can pulverize the ore, smelt and alloy on the way. Craftable items now show in every terminal: click one marked Craft (or Ctrl + click any item with a green +), pick an amount, check the plan and press Start. You get a chat message when it's done. The Jobs button (bottom-right of any terminal) lists every job with its progress and a Cancel button.

entries.text: Records recipes onto Blank Patterns. The C/P button switches between two kinds. CRAFTING: lay out a crafting-table recipe by clicking items into the grid (copies only - nothing is used up) or press + on a crafting recipe in JEI; the result shows on the right. With the S button on (Substitutes), the pattern accepts every item the recipe allows in each slot - any planks, any cobblestone. PROCESSING: a machine recipe with amounts - left-click a slot with a stack to set that amount, right-click to add one - up to 3 item outputs on the right, and a row of fluid slots underneath: click them with a bucket or tank to set a fluid or gas in or out (right-click adds another container's worth). JEI's + fills all of it from machine recipes, fluids included. Then put a Blank Pattern in the top-right slot, press Encode and take the pattern from the slot below. In Processing mode the lightning-bolt button fills any energy item in the outputs to full charge - with the same item as the input, that's a charging pattern for a Charger. Crafting patterns don't care about charge: a charged jetpack or battery box in storage is used just like an empty one (enchanted or renamed items never are). Processing mode also has a Machine slot (right of the grid): click it with the machine the recipe runs in. Patterns kept in an Assembly Matrix need it so the network knows which machines to use; JEI's + fills it in for this mod's machines, furnaces and smithing. Machine patterns accept any item of the same material: a pattern made with Iron Ore also takes Deepslate Iron Ore (and other mods' iron ore), raw materials, dusts and ingots likewise.
Encode a recipe onto it in a Pattern Encoder. A Crafting Pattern can be wiped back to blank with sneak + right-click in the air.

Does the work for autocrafting: holds up to 9 patterns, plus Speed and Efficiency upgrade slots. Crafting patterns are crafted inside it - one craft every 8 ticks, plus one more per Speed Upgrade (up to 5 at once). Processing patterns are done by the MACHINE TOUCHING the assembler: it sends the item and fluid inputs in and pulls the item, fluid and gas results back into storage, like AE2's Pattern Provider. Tips: the machine's face touching the assembler must be In + Out (the default), and turn the machine's auto-output off so the results wait for the assembler. Built-in smelting: put an assembler against an Electric Furnace and the network knows every furnace recipe without patterns - a missing Iron Ingot is smelted from raw iron, iron ore or iron dust in storage (your own patterns always come first). Machines that use water, like the Ore Purifier, get it from their own Sink or pipe, so water is never 'missing' from a plan.  It works against any face of this mod's machines - the machine's Sides settings don't apply to assemblers - and several assemblers can share one machine. Its glass case shows the crafting core inside, which lights up while it works. Once you build an Assembly Matrix, assemblers (and the simpler Machine Connector) also run the Matrix's patterns on the machines they touch.

Runs crafting jobs - one job at a time per CPU; extra requests wait in a queue. Right-click it to see every job and how far along it is; sneak + right-click to cancel them (anything already crafted stays in storage). A network needs at least one CPU and one Molecular Assembler to autocraft. When a job is stuck, the Jobs screen says exactly why: the machine it's waiting on (with its position), the ingredient it needs, or that no assembler holds the pattern. In a terminal's Jobs screen, click a job to see each of its steps: how many are left, how many are running, and on which machine. Tiers: a Basic CPU runs 1 job at a time, Advanced 2, Elite 4, Quantum 8 - raise it with Crafting Upgrades. It keeps its tier when broken.

Right-click a Crafting CPU, Crafting Accelerator or Machine Connector of the tier below to make it Advanced. Tiers go in order: Basic, Advanced, Elite, Quantum. The block keeps its tier when broken, and a glowing light strip shows the tier.

Right-click a Crafting CPU, Crafting Accelerator or Machine Connector of the tier below to make it Elite. Tiers go in order: Basic, Advanced, Elite, Quantum. The block keeps its tier when broken, and a glowing light strip shows the tier.

Right-click a Crafting CPU, Crafting Accelerator or Machine Connector of the tier below to make it Quantum. Tiers go in order: Basic, Advanced, Elite, Quantum. The block keeps its tier when broken, and a glowing light strip shows the tier.

The Assembly Matrix is a central pattern store for your whole network. Build a box from 3x3x3 up to 7x7x7 out of Matrix Casing (Matrix Glass works too, so you can see inside), with one Matrix Controller in a wall. Then swap any wall blocks for Pattern Banks (27 patterns each) and Crafting Accelerators - they can also go inside the box, and empty space inside is fine. Connect any part of it to the storage network with Storage Cable. Right-click the controller to store patterns: each page is one Pattern Bank. Crafting patterns are made inside the Matrix itself - 2 crafts per cycle, plus 2 per Crafting Accelerator. Processing patterns run on ANY machine of the right type that has a Molecular Assembler or a Machine Connector touching it, anywhere on the network - so two furnaces with connectors run your smelting twice as fast without copying a single pattern. Every processing pattern in the Matrix needs its Machine set in the Pattern Encoder (JEI's + does it for this mod's machines). The screen says what's wrong if the box isn't right. The controller's screen also lists every machine the Matrix can use (a panel on the right). Put at least one Pattern Bank inside before storing patterns. To set (or change) which machine a processing pattern uses, click the pattern in the controller's screen while holding that machine's item - hovering a pattern with no machine reminds you.
Part of an Assembly Matrix: holds 27 patterns, filled from the Matrix Controller's screen (one bank per page). Put it in place of any wall block, or inside the box. Drops its patterns if broken.

Part of an Assembly Matrix: each one adds 2 crafts per cycle for the Matrix's crafting patterns. Put it in place of any wall block, or inside the box. Tiers: +2 crafts per cycle (Basic), +4 (Advanced), +8 (Elite), +16 (Quantum) - raise it with Crafting Upgrades. A Matrix tops out at 256 crafts per cycle.

A Quantum-tier Assembly Matrix part. It adds 16 crafts per cycle like a Quantum Crafting Accelerator, and while the Matrix is running jobs, every machine it crafts with (through Machine Connectors, buses and assemblers) runs as if it had 2 more Speed upgrades - up to 8 more from 4 Overclock Accelerators. Overclocked machines use more power, just like with Speed upgrades. Made from a Quantum Crafting Accelerator.
The frame and walls of an Assembly Matrix. Matrix Glass can replace it in the walls (not needed on edges).
See-through wall block for an Assembly Matrix.

A flat Molecular Assembler: the same 9 pattern slots, screen, Speed Upgrades and everything else, but as a thin panel stuck onto a machine's face instead of a whole block. Sneak + right-click to place it on a machine (a plain right-click would open the machine), then connect Storage Cable to it. Turn a Molecular Assembler into a panel in the crafting grid, and back again.

A flat panel that connects a machine to the storage network so the Assembly Matrix can use it - like a Molecular Assembler with no pattern slots and no screen. Sneak + right-click to stick it onto any face of a machine (plain right-click would open the machine), then run Storage Cable to the panel. The Matrix's patterns for that kind of machine run there, up to 4 operations per cycle, and the Matrix Controller's screen lists every connected machine. Early on, use Molecular Assemblers (patterns live in each one); once you have a Matrix, switch to Connectors. On an Electric Furnace it also enables built-in smelting. Tiers: 4 operations per cycle (Basic), 8 (Advanced), 16 (Elite), 32 (Quantum) - raise it with Crafting Upgrades. It keeps its tier when broken.

Keeps items in stock automatically. Click one of its 9 slots with an item to add it (keeps 64 to start); click the slot to select it, type an amount and press Set, or x to remove it. Every 5 seconds, if storage has fewer than the target and nothing is already being made, it starts a crafting job for the difference - so ask it to keep 256 Superconductor Ingots and it quietly tops them up. The bar under each slot: green = in stock, blue = crafting, red = can't craft (missing ingredients or no pattern).

categories.title: Creative tools
categories.intro: Only in the creative tab, for testing builds: unlimited power and unlimited storage.

entries.text: Creative mode only. Unlimited power: it pushes as much as anything next to it will take every tick, and cables can draw as much as they like. Handy for testing builds.
Creative mode only. A storage disk with practically unlimited room (still 63 item types).
Creative mode only. A fluid disk with practically unlimited room (still 63 fluid and gas types).

categories.title: Monitoring and control
categories.intro: See where your power goes, and let redstone switch things for you. Both Fission Reactors also give comparators a signal for their heat - set a reactor's redstone mode and it can throttle itself.

entries.text: Right-click a cable to see its whole network: power coming in, power going to machines, power going into storage, and how much is stored. Right-click any other block - including other mods' machines and batteries - to see its stored energy, what it's generating right now and what's in its tanks. Machines don't open their screens when you use it, so it's safe to click around. On an item pipe it lists every connection (Push or Pull), what each Pull connection can take out, and whether each Push destination would accept it - the quickest way to find out why items aren't moving. On a machine it also lists each face's setting and what an Out face has ready.

Goes in a cable line. Power goes in the LEFT side and out the RIGHT side as you look at its screen (the top shows an arrow). The screen shows FE per tick and a running total; right-click for the peak as well, sneak + right-click to reset. A redstone signal switches the flow off, so it doubles as a power switch for a whole branch of your base. A comparator next to it gets a stronger signal the more power flows.

Place it touching any cable and its screen shows that whole cable network: In (generators and discharging batteries), Use (machines), Chg (going into batteries) and how full the batteries are. Right-click for the full readout. A comparator reads how full the batteries are, 0-15: put a comparator and a redstone torch between it and a Coal Generator set to run on redstone, and the generator only burns fuel when your batteries run low. Right-click it to open a history graph: power generated (green), power used (red) and battery fill (blue) over the last 10 minutes or 2 hours - hover the graph for exact values. Sneak + right-click for the quick readout.

categories.title: Gases and steam
categories.intro: Hydrogen, oxygen and steam travel in Gas Pipes and can be kept in Fluid Tanks. Split water into hydrogen and oxygen, burn it later for power, or put spare steam to work.

entries.text: Splits water into hydrogen and oxygen using power. Pulls water from a Sink, Electric Pump or pipes and pushes both gases out into Gas Pipes, Fluid Tanks or a Gas Burner Generator. Put a Hydrogen Jetpack in its slot to refuel it. Speed and Efficiency Upgrades work here.

Burns gas for power, up to 40 mB per tick. Hydrogen gives 7 FE per mB (9 with half as much oxygen); methane from a Bio-Digester gives 12 FE per mB (15 with the same amount of oxygen). Hydrogen is burned first if both are piped in. Making hydrogen costs more power than burning it gives back, so think of hydrogen as a way to store and move energy - methane, on the other hand, is free fuel from farm waste. Idles when full, so no gas is wasted.

A cheap, early steam generator with no spin-up. Put it next to a Boiler, a Fission Reactor or a Gas Pipe carrying steam. The Steam Turbine gets twice as much out of the same steam, so this is the step before it.
Runs Pulverizer recipes (ore doubling, gravel, sand and more) on steam instead of power. A good use for spare Boiler or reactor steam. Speed Upgrades make it faster and use more steam.
Flies like the Advanced Jetpack but burns hydrogen instead of FE, and a full tank lasts a long time. Refuel it by putting it in a Gas Electrolyzer's slot (a Charger won't fill it).

Powered armour for the end game - tougher than netherite, and it never wears out because it runs on energy. Each piece stores its own charge: put it in a Charger, or just stand near a Wireless Charger while wearing it. Helmet: night vision and water breathing (20 FE/t). Chestplate: the fastest jetpack in the mod - hold jump to fly (120 FE/t while thrusting). Leggings: a speed boost (10 FE/t). Boots: no fall damage, and you step up full blocks without jumping. Energy shield: every charged piece absorbs 22.5% of the damage you take - 90% with the full suit - at 1,000 FE per point of damage absorbed. When a piece runs dry it's still strong armour, just without its powers. Each piece is made from its netherite version, Quantum Alloy and a Quantum Power Core; the chestplate also needs an Advanced Jetpack. The whole suit can be autocrafted: the netherite pieces through a Smithing Press, the rest through crafting and Alloy Smelter patterns.
The heart of each Quantum Suit piece: 4 Quantum Alloy, 4 Superconductor Ingots and an Ultimate Battery Box (a charged one is fine).

Quantum Suit modules add powers to the suit. Wear the right piece and right-click a module to fit it; press the Suit Modules key (V by default) to switch each one on or off or take it out again (you get the module back). They run on the charge of the piece they're in. Magnet (chestplate): pulls dropped items and XP orbs to you from 8 blocks away - hold sneak to pause it. Flight (chestplate): creative-style flight while charged - double-tap jump; 100 FE/t while flying. Auto-Feed (helmet): eats the most filling safe food in your inventory whenever you're hungry. Jump Boost (leggings): jump about three blocks high. Water Walking (boots): walk on water; sneak to go under. Each is made from Quantum Alloy, superconductor, a redstone block and one key item (lodestone, elytra, golden carrot, slime block, lily pad). Radiation Shielding (chestplate): blocks all radiation, when radiation is switched on in the config.
Quantum Suit chestplate module: heals you over time while you're hurt (Regeneration I). 800 FE a second while healing.
Quantum Suit leggings module: Resistance I - a fifth off all damage. 200 FE a second.
Quantum Suit helmet module: cures poison, wither, hunger, nausea, blindness, darkness, weakness and slowness as soon as they hit. 500 FE per cure.
Quantum Suit helmet module: Haste II - mine and swing faster. 200 FE a second.
Quantum Suit leggings module: fire and lava don't hurt you while it's charged. 300 FE a second while you're burning.
Quantum Suit boots module: you turn invisible while you sneak. 200 FE a second while sneaking.
A Quantum Suit chestplate module: Flight uses a quarter of the power (25 FE/t). Made from a Flight Module, Aether Crystals and Cryonite Shards.

Radiation is optional and OFF by default - turn it on in the mod's config file ([radiation] enabled = true; strength sets how harsh it is). With it on, running fission reactors give off radiation within 16 blocks (much stronger up close), and carrying nuclear materials is radioactive too: depleted fuel rods most of all, then plutonium, MOX and uranium fuel rods, and a little from uranium itself. Your dose builds up while you're exposed and slowly fades once you're clear; dying resets it. At 100 rad you get nausea, at 300 weakness and hunger, at 600 poison, and from 1,000 rad you take damage. Protection: each piece of the Hazmat Suit (yellow wool and leather) blocks 25% - wear all four for full protection - or fit the Radiation Shielding Module to a Quantum Chestplate for complete protection. Hold the Geiger Counter to see the radiation reaching you (after shielding) and your dose - it clicks faster the hotter it gets. Iodine Tablets (salt and dried kelp) remove 300 rad each.

Makes fusion fuel from water: it pulls the heavy hydrogen (deuterium) out, 50 mB of water for every 1 mB of deuterium gas, 2 mB each tick. Feed it water from a Sink, Pump or pipes and pipe the deuterium to your Fusion Reactor - or put it right next to one. Speed Upgrades make it faster. Takes power through the bottom.

Breeds tritium, the other fusion fuel, from lithium - using the neutrons of a running Fission Reactor. Place it against a single-block Fission Reactor or a multiblock's Fission Controller and give it lithium ingots: each one becomes 250 mB of tritium gas (one fusion fuel pair) in 20 seconds while the reactor is running. It needs no power of its own. Pipe the tritium to your Fusion Reactor.
stats: a running fission reactor next to it

entries.text: Splits air into nitrogen and oxygen with nothing but power - no water, no fuel. Each tick it makes 16 mB of nitrogen and 4 mB of oxygen (about the real mix of air) and pushes both into Gas Pipes. It needs at least one side open to the air. Nitrogen feeds Cryo Injectors; oxygen boosts Gas Burner Generators.

Nitrogen cooling for fission. Place it against a Fission Reactor or a Fission Controller and pipe nitrogen in from an Air Separator: while it feeds 20 mB of nitrogen per tick, the reactor makes 50% more power. It only uses nitrogen while the reactor is running.

A screen for your fission reactor. On a multiblock reactor, build it straight into the wall in place of any Fission Casing or Glass block (not edges or corners) - the controller links it when the reactor forms, so it works anywhere on the walls. On a single-block Fission Reactor, just place it against the reactor. Its face shows the heat (green, orange near the limit, red when hot), the power it's making, whether it's running, idle or SCRAMmed, and any add-ons fitted (Neutron Reflector, nitrogen cooling). A comparator next to it reads the heat from 0 to 15 - wire it to the reactor's redstone setting and it can throttle itself before it overheats. It works on Fusion Reactors too: there it shows the plasma temperature, output and plasma tier, and can be built into the fusion multiblock's wall in the same way.

Bounces stray neutrons back into the core, so fuel rods last 50% longer. Right-click a Fission Reactor or Fission Controller to fit one; it shows in Jade and on a Reactor Gauge, and drops back out if the reactor is broken.

Upgrades a Fusion Reactor's plasma. Right-click a Fusion Reactor or a multiblock's Fusion Controller with Mk I, then Mk II, then Mk III (in that order). Mk I doubles the reactor's output, Mk II triples it and Mk III quadruples it. Fuel burns faster too (x1.5, x2, x2.5), but always less than the output gain - so every tier gets more power out of each deuterium + tritium pair. At the higher tiers, pipe the fuel in as gas (Isotope Separator and Tritium Breeder) so it keeps up. Jade and a Reactor Gauge show the tier; the coils drop back out if the reactor is broken.

Makes antimatter for the Antimatter Reactor by smashing fusion fuel together at enormous energies. Each operation turns 10 mB of deuterium + 10 mB of tritium + 20,000 FE into 1 mB of antimatter - one a tick, more with Speed Upgrades. Pipe deuterium (Isotope Separator) and tritium (Tritium Breeder) in with Gas Pipes and feed it power from below (Quantum Cable is ideal); it pushes antimatter out into Gas Pipes, or straight into an Antimatter Reactor next to it.

The end-game power source. It annihilates antimatter for 50,000 FE per mB - 2.5 times what the Particle Collider spent making it - burning up to 20 mB a tick for up to 1,000,000 FE/t. It holds 50 million FE, pushes power out of every side, and idles (burning nothing) while its buffer is full. Pipe antimatter in from a Particle Collider, or place the two side by side. Its core glows and pulses while it burns.

The first step of rocket fuel: chills a gas into a liquid using nitrogen as the coolant. Pipe in methane (from a Bio-Digester) or oxygen (from an Air Separator or electrolyzer) plus nitrogen (Air Separator): each operation turns 40 mB of gas + 4 mB of nitrogen + 200 FE into 20 mB of Liquid Methane or Liquid Oxygen. It works on one gas at a time - use a Fluid Filter on its pipe, or one condenser per gas. The liquid comes out into ordinary Fluid Pipes (liquids don't go in Gas Pipes).

Blends methalox Rocket Fuel - the same mix real rockets burn: 10 mB Liquid Methane + 20 mB Liquid Oxygen + 100 FE = 30 mB Rocket Fuel, every tick (faster with Speed Upgrades). A Rocket needs 16,000 mB, which takes about 5,300 mB of Liquid Methane and 10,700 mB of Liquid Oxygen - roughly 135 crops' worth of methane through a Bio-Digester.

The rocket for the satellite program, put together from parts made in your existing machines: Hull Plates pressed in a Compressor (4 steel plates each), a Rocket Engine upgraded from a Rocket Nozzle in a Smithing Press (netherite upgrade template + Quantum Alloy), Fuel Tank Sections (Hull Plates around a Quantum Fluid Tank), a Guidance Computer (Storage Terminals and a Molecular Assembler) and a Nose Cone. It needs 16,000 mB of Rocket Fuel and a payload such as a Solar Satellite. Launch it from a Launch Controller and Launch Pad.

A Rocket payload: Quantum Solar Panels, superconductor and a Quantum Power Core. Once in orbit it will beam steady power - day and night, in any weather - down to a Receiver Dish - right-click a dish to claim it.

The brain of a launch site. Build a 3x3 square of Launch Pads (steel deck plates with hazard stripes), put at least one Launch Tower (a steel lattice) right beside the pad, and place the Launch Controller (a desk console) touching the pad. Open the controller: put a Rocket in the top slot - it appears standing on the middle of the pad - and a Solar Satellite in the payload slot, then pipe 16,000 mB of Rocket Fuel into the controller. A checklist shows what's still missing (launch site, rocket, payload, fuel, clear sky). Press LAUNCH: a 10 second countdown appears for everyone nearby, then the rocket lifts off in fire and smoke and climbs out of sight - and a moment later the satellite reaches orbit (the whole server is told). The screen also shows how many satellites are in orbit and how many are linked to dishes. You can also right-click the controller with buckets of Rocket Fuel (16 fill a rocket) - handy in creative for testing.
stats: 3 x 3 Launch Pads + a Launch Tower

entries.text: A steel deck plate with hazard stripes. Nine of them in a 3x3 make the pad for a Launch Controller; the rocket stands on the middle one. They're only 4 pixels high.
An open steel lattice tower section. Put at least one beside the Launch Pad - stack more for a proper gantry.

Collects the power a Solar Satellite in orbit beams down: about 100,000 FE/t, day and night, in any weather - no fuel, ever. Right-click it to claim one of your satellites that isn't already linked to a dish; sneak + right-click to release it again. It holds 10 million FE and pushes power out of every side. Launch more satellites and build more dishes for more power. Jade shows its satellite and output.

The Orbital Mining Laser. Build a Mining Satellite (Quantum Solar Panels, superconductor, a Diamond Laser Lens and a Quantum Power Core) and launch it from a Launch Pad like a Solar Satellite. Then place a Laser Drill under open sky: it automatically claims one of your free Mining Satellites, and while it has power the satellite fires a laser beam down from orbit onto the drill - you can see it from far away - and drills out one ore every second (2,000,000 FE each, about 100,000 FE/t: one Solar Satellite and Receiver Dish can run one drill). The ores come from the forge:ores tag, so other mods' ores turn up too; common ores are common and diamonds, emeralds and uranium are rare. Put Laser Lenses (iron, copper, gold, redstone, diamond, uranium) in its input slots to make that ore ten times as likely - several lenses stack. Ores go into its output grid and then into chests, pipes or buses next to it. Item Filters work in its input slots too: set one to Block and the drill never makes those ores - in Name mode one deepslate ore blocks every deepslate_... ore.

Oxygen-blown steelmaking - how real steelworks do it: oxygen is blown through iron to burn off the carbon. 1 iron ingot (or iron dust) + 100 mB of oxygen = 1 steel ingot in 3 seconds, using 80 FE/t and no coal - much faster than blasting, and cheaper than the Alloy Smelter route. Pipe oxygen in from an Air Separator or Gas Electrolyzer. Speed Upgrades make it faster. Takes Tier Installers: 3, 5, 7, 9 or 12 at once.

Turns farm waste into fuel. Crops, seeds, saplings, leaves, flowers, rotten flesh, kelp, cactus and other plant or animal matter rot down into methane (biogas): 200 mB per item, one every 2 seconds, with no power needed. Pipe the methane to a Gas Burner Generator, where it's worth 12 FE per mB (15 with oxygen) - a cheap early way into gas power, and a use for all that spare seed and sapling clutter.

A powered smithing table, so autocrafting can do smithing: netherite upgrades, armour trims and other mods' smithing recipes, 5 seconds each at 60 FE/t. It has a slot each for the template, the item to upgrade and the material, and only takes an item into the slot a recipe uses it in - so pipes and Molecular Assemblers can feed it. For autocrafting, make a processing pattern from the smithing recipe (JEI's + on the vanilla smithing recipe works) and give it to an assembler touching the press. Speed Upgrades make it faster. Takes Tier Installers: 3, 5, 7, 9 or 12 at once.

An electric brewing stand built for automation. Put glass bottles - or water bottles or potions - in its three bottle slots and an ingredient (nether wart, sugar, a spider eye...) in the slot above. It fills glass bottles with water from its own 4,000 mB tank (333 mB each - pipe water in, or right-click with a water bucket), then brews all three bottles with one ingredient in 5 seconds at 20 FE/t - no blaze powder needed. It uses the game's brewing recipes, so every vanilla potion works, including splash and lingering, and modded brewing too. Feed bottles and ingredients in from the top or sides; finished potions come out of the bottom. For autocrafting, JEI's + on a brewing recipe makes a pattern for three bottles at once with the Brewing Machine set as its machine.

The opposite of the Electric Pump: it puts fluid into the world. Pipe a fluid in (or right-click with a bucket) and give it power, and it fills the open space below and around it with source blocks - one every half second, using 1,000 mB and 100 FE each - spreading outwards and downwards up to 32 blocks away, but never above its own level. Fill a moat, flood a hole, or lay down lava for a lava farm. Works with any fluid that can exist as a block (water, lava and modded liquids). Jade shows how many blocks it has placed and when it's finished.

Moves blocks that hold things without emptying them. Right-click a chest, machine, tank or any block with contents: it's picked up - everything inside included - and the Block Mover glows while it holds it. Right-click a surface to put it down again. Great for rearranging a base without unloading every chest. It respects storage network security and won't pick up unbreakable blocks.

A handheld scanner: right-click to list every kind of ore within 16 blocks of you, how many there are, and the direction and distance to the nearest of each (for example '7 blocks north-east, 4 down'). Finds other mods' ores too. 5,000 FE per scan from its 1,000,000 FE battery - charge it in a Charger or near a Wireless Charger.

Breaks the block in front of it once a second, as if mined with a diamond pickaxe, and keeps the drops - 400 FE per block. The drops go into chests, pipes or Import Buses next to it. Set its redstone mode to break only on a signal. Pair it with a Block Placer, or put it in front of a cobblestone generator for endless cobblestone.

Places blocks from its 3 input slots in front of it, twice a second - 100 FE per block. Feed it from a pipe or an Export Bus. Together with a Block Breaker it makes a simple stone or cobblestone farm, or moves blocks along a line.

A hands-off wood supply. It works a 9x9 patch in front of it at its own level: plants saplings from its inputs on dirt or grass, grows them faster with bone meal if you give it some, and fells grown trees - every connected log and leaf - keeping the logs, saplings, sticks and apples. Give it a few saplings to start; it replants from what it collects if you pipe the saplings back in. 200 FE per job; Speed Upgrades help.

Looks after animals on a 9x9 area in front of it. It breeds pairs with feed from its inputs (wheat for cows and sheep, seeds for chickens, carrots for pigs... - up to 24 animals in the area), shears sheep for wool, milks cows into empty buckets, and picks up eggs and feathers. Fence the animals in front of it. 200 FE per job.

categories.title: Fluids
categories.intro: Water and lava on tap, and somewhere to keep them.

entries.text: Endless water. Pushes water into any tank, pipe or machine next to it and fills buckets. Needs no water source and no power.

Place it above a lake or lava pool - it looks straight down through air to find the fluid. Pumps from anywhere in the connected fluid within 32 blocks. Water is left in place (it never runs out); lava and other fluids are removed. Pushes what it pumps into tanks, pipes or machines beside or above it. Upgradable: Speed and Energy upgrades as usual, and Tier Installers make it pump 3, 5, 7, 9 or 12 buckets per cycle (Advanced to Naquadah), with a tank that grows to match (up to 192,000 mB), a reach of up to 128 blocks and faster output.
stats: 1/3/5/7/9/12 buckets per cycle, up to 192,000 mB and 128 blocks

entries.text: Holds one fluid. The fluid level shows through the glass (lava glows). Buckets and pipes work on any side; keeps its contents when mined; comparators read how full it is. Right-click with an empty hand to see what's inside.
Advanced tank.
Elite tank.
Ultimate tank.
Tier 5 tank.

categories.title: Automation
categories.intro: Machines that work the world for you.

entries.text: Mines an area layer by layer. Settings in its GUI: area size (3x3 to 65x65), centred on the quarry or behind it, how deep to dig (shift-click for 10 at a time), and tool mode - Normal, Silk Touch or Fortune III (50% more power). Items in the Void slots are thrown away. Skips fluids, unbreakable blocks and anything with an inventory, so it never destroys chests or spawners. Items go to its buffer and are pushed into neighbouring chests or pipes. To choose exactly where it digs, use a Quarry Planner. It sends what it mines out through the faces set to Out in its Sides window - pipes, chests, or an Import Bus.

A quarry that only takes what you ask for. Tell it which ores to find with Item Filters in its slots - for example one set to Allow and Tag mode holding a diamond ore takes every diamond ore, deepslate ones included; with no filter it takes every ore. Put an Enchanted Book of Silk Touch, or of Fortune I to III, in a slot to choose how they're mined - the book is a setting and isn't used up. It scans a 33x33 area under itself layer by layer, from just below the machine down to the bottom of the world, and mines only the wanted ores - up to 4 a second at 800 FE each - leaving the stone and everything else exactly where it was. Ores go into its output grid and out to chests, pipes or buses next to it. Change the filters or the book and it starts scanning again from the top. Jade shows how many ores it has mined and which layer it's on. Keep the area loaded with a Chunk Loader. It's built like a proper drilling rig - a base plate, corner struts, a radar screen and an antenna, with its drill going into the ground.

Tends a 9x9 area around itself at its own height. Harvests and replants ripe wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot and nether wart; harvests melons and pumpkins; cuts sugar cane and cactus, leaving the bottom block to regrow. Its three seed slots plant empty spots on its own level: crop seeds on farmland, nether wart on soul sand, melon and pumpkin seeds on farmland, cactus on sand, and Sugar Cane Seeds (or sugar cane) on sand, dirt or grass that has water right beside it - or on Irrigated Sand under a Sprinkler, with no water channel needed. Like crops, they sit on the ground one block below the farmer's level. Fertilizer or bone meal goes in the slot on the far left. The farmer grows each plant that is still growing by one step as it passes; one Fertilizer is good for 32 steps and bone meal for 8, so a stack of Fertilizer lasts a long time. Put it next to a storage cable and it restocks itself from your storage network: Fertilizer (or bone meal) and more of the seeds already in its slots. Harvest is pushed into neighbouring chests.

Part of the greenhouse system. Hang Sprinklers from the ceiling (or put one on top of a post) above your crops and pipe water in, or right-click with a water bucket: each uses 20 mB of water a second, keeps every farmland block in a 9x9 area up to 6 blocks below it wet, and gives the plants a 15% chance of an extra growth step every second - with a little shower of water. Pair it with a Grow Lamp for even faster growth, and a Crop Farmer to plant and harvest.

A powered lamp for the greenhouse: hang it above the crops and connect power (40 FE/t). It gives full light, so crops grow indoors, underground and at night, and gives plants in a 9x9 area up to 6 blocks below a 10% chance of an extra growth step every second. Its bulb glows while it has power.

Three bone meal in one (2 bone meal + rotten flesh + dirt makes 4). Right-click a plant to grow it a lot, or put it in a Crop Farmer's fertilizer slot: it then fertilises everything still growing as it passes - crops, melon and pumpkin stems, sugar cane, cactus and nether wart - one growth step each, 32 steps per Fertilizer. With Sprinklers and Grow Lamps overhead, a greenhouse turns out crops very quickly - feed the surplus to a Bio-Digester for methane.

One sugar cane makes two. Plant them like sugar cane: on sand, dirt or grass with water right beside that block (not on top of it) - or on Irrigated Sand under a Sprinkler, no water needed. The Crop Farmer plants them too.

Sand for greenhouses: sugar cane grows on it without a water channel, as long as a Sprinkler with water in it is overhead (within 4 blocks sideways and up to 8 blocks above). Water beside it works too, like normal sand, and cactus grows on it. It doesn't fall. Lay it where the farmland would go, in reach of the Crop Farmer, and the farmer plants Sugar Cane Seeds on it. 8 sand around a water bucket makes 8 (you get the bucket back).
stats: grows under a Sprinkler, no water needed

entries.text: Green-framed glass for building the greenhouse's walls and roof (8 from glass and green dye).

Crafts one recipe over and over. Click items into its 3x3 pattern to set the recipe - they're ghost items and aren't used up. Ingredients are pulled from chests next to it; leftovers like empty buckets go back into a neighbouring inventory.

Keeps a square of chunks around it loaded while powered, so your reactor, quarry and farms run while you're away. Click the size button for a bigger area, right-click it for a smaller one: up to 5x5 chunks, or 7x7, 9x9, 11x11 and 15x15 with Advanced, Elite, Ultimate and Quantum Tier Installers. Costs power per chunk loaded. Releases the chunks when it runs out of power, is switched off with redstone, or is broken.

Launches up to 4 Utility Drones and gives them work. Click the mode button: Harvest picks ripe crops within 12 blocks and replants them; Collect picks up dropped items within 12 blocks; Fetch brings items here from a linked inventory; Deliver takes items from here to a linked inventory (link one with a Drone Remote, up to 64 blocks away). Whatever the drones bring back goes into the station's 15 slots, which pipes, hoppers, belts and buses can empty. Uses 20 FE/t for each drone out working. Redstone control pauses it and calls the drones home.
Put it in a Drone Station's drone slots and it flies out to work - harvesting, collecting, fetching or delivering, depending on the station's mode. Drones fly through anything and can't be hurt.
Links a Drone Station to an inventory for Fetch and Deliver: right-click the chest (or machine), then right-click the station. Sneak + right-click a station to clear its link.

Picks up a whole cube of blocks and puts it down somewhere else. Insert a Spatial Cell and a cube outline appears on top of the projector, centred over it (3, 7 or 15 wide, by the cell). Press Capture: every block in the cube - chests and machines with everything in them - goes into the cell and leaves air. Carry the cell to another projector (or move this one), make sure the outlined area is empty, and press Deploy to put it all back exactly as it was. Costs 40 FE per block moved. Can't capture unbreakable blocks like bedrock.
